2.w: “Oh, if only my grief could be weighed, and my misfortune laid on the scales too!

3.w: But because it is heavier than the sand of the sea, that is why my words have been wild.

4.w: For the arrows of the Almighty are within me; my spirit drinks their poison; God’s sudden terrors are arrayed against me.

5.w: “Does the wild donkey bray when it is near grass? Or does the ox bellow over its fodder?

6.w: Can food that is tasteless be eaten without salt? Or is there any taste in the white of an egg?

7.w: I have refused to touch such things; they are like loathsome food to me.

8.w: “Oh that my request would be realized, and that God would grant me what I long for!

9.w: And that God would be willing to crush me, that he would let loose his hand and kill me.

10.w: Then I would yet have my comfort, then I would rejoice, in spite of pitiless pain, for I have not concealed the words of the Holy One.

11.w: What is my strength, that I should wait? And what is my end, that I should prolong my life?

12.w: Is my strength like that of stones? Or is my flesh made of bronze?

13.w: Is not my power to help myself nothing, and has not every resource been driven from me?

14.w: “To the one in despair, kindness should come from his friend even if he forsakes the fear of the Almighty.

15.w: My brothers have been as treacherous as a seasonal stream, and as the riverbeds of the intermittent streams that flow away.

16.w: They are dark because of ice; snow is piled up over them.

17.w: When they are scorched, they dry up, when it is hot, they vanish from their place.

18.w: Caravans turn aside from their routes; they go into the wasteland and perish.

19.w: The caravans of Tema looked intently for these streams; the traveling merchants of Sheba hoped for them.

20.w: They were distressed because each one had been so confident; they arrived there, but were disappointed.

21.w: For now you have become like these streams that are no help; you see a terror and are afraid.

22.w: “Have I ever said, ‘Give me something, and from your fortune make gifts in my favor’?

23.w: Or, ‘Deliver me from the enemy’s power, and from the hand of tyrants ransom me’?

24.w: “Teach me, and I, for my part, will be silent; explain to me how I have been mistaken.

25.w: How painful are honest words! But what does your reproof prove?

26.w: Do you intend to criticize mere words, and treat the words of a despairing man as wind?

27.w: Yes, you would gamble for the fatherless, and auction off your friend.

28.w: “Now then, be good enough to look at me; and I will not lie to your face!

29.w: Relent, let there be no falsehood; reconsider, for my righteousness is intact!

30.w: Is there any falsehood on my lips? Can my mouth not discern evil things?
